What falls in it: Safety components of products (or products themselves) under EU product law that must undergo third-party conformity assessment, such as many medical devices
What follows: Provider: risk management, testing, documentation, conformity assessment. Deployer: use as instructed, human oversight, logs

What falls in it: Uses in eight areas: biometrics; critical infrastructure; education; employment; essential public and private services, such as benefits; law enforcement; migration and border control; justice and democratic processes
What follows: As above; public bodies also assess the impact on fundamental rights, except for critical infrastructure
Who decides: The provider, which may classify the system out (next row)

What falls in it: A listed system that "does not pose a significant risk of harm", which applies only where it meets one of four conditions: it is intended "to perform a narrow procedural task", to improve completed human work, to spot patterns without replacing human assessment, or to do preparatory work. Profiling people is always high-risk
What follows: The provider documents its own assessment and registers; the assessment is shown only "upon request"

What falls in it: Systems such as chatbots and AI-generated content
What follows: Tell people they are interacting with AI (chatbots); mark AI-generated content as such and disclose deep fakes and AI text published on matters of public interest
Outside the high-risk requirements; other applicable duties may remain.
